This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 15-09-2024 at about 3-00 to 03-05 am., the petitioner was traveling in Toyota Etios Car bearing Reg.No.TN-05-AJ-7176 along with his friends from Bengaluru towards Burnout cafe Kaggalipura side on Bengaluru- Kanakapura road and when they reached near Saluhunase village, Uttrahalli Hobli, Bengaluru south,
Bengaluru, the driver of the said vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the road side tree, result of which the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to General Hospital,
Kaggalipura and ST.Martha's Hospital, Saluhunase wherein 1st aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to T.R Hospital & Research Foundation, Trichy wherein admitted as an inpatient from 16-09-2024 to 30-09-2024 and after further management petitioner has took treatment at Kauvery Hospital as well as Santhigiri Ayurveda & Siddha Hospital.
So far, the petitioner has spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical expenses, nourishment and conveyance.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 20 years.
He was studying in MBA 1st Sem at Jain CMS Business School, Sheshadri road, Bengaluru and was doing part time work at medical store/stationary ship, Bengaluru and earning sum of Rs.20,000/-.
Due to the permanent disability petitioner cannot concentrate on his studies due to the head injuries sustained by him.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Toyota Etios Car bearing Reg.No.TN-05-AJ-7176 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed Ex-parte.

5. The respondent No.2/the insurer of Etios Car bearing Reg.No.TN-05-AJ-7176 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid driving licence and not wearing seatbelt.

It is further contended that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident, that the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gain.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:

sentences.text: 1.Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries on account of road traffic accident on 15-09-2024 at about 03-20 to 03-50 am., at Saluhunaase village, Bengaluru - Kanakapura road, Uttrahalli Hobli, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Toyota Etios car bearing Reg.No.TN-15-AJ-7176 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

7. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and one witness as P.W.2 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.
The respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

11. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P7 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, Notice u/Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon, etc.
12.

sentences.text: So far as the contention taken by the respondent no.2 to the effect that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the policy condition by using the said vehicle for commercial purpose is concerned, admittedly the said vehicle is a private vehicle.
It is the definite case of the petitioners that on the date of accident the petitioner and his friends were been to Burnout Cafe at Kaggalipura to celebrate the birthday party of their friend.
Including driver, all the inmates of the offending vehicle are the friends.
The police documents makes it clear that the vehicle in question is a private vehicle and it was used for private purpose but not for commercial purpose for hire.
Hence, there is no violation of policy condition and there is no iota of evidence placed by the respondent no.2 to say that the said vehicle was used for commercial purpose.
14. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, it is proved that petitioner was the inmate in the offending vehicle and Mukesh was the driver of the said vehicle.
In the complaint and the statement of the witnesses it is stated that the petitioner was the inmate of the said vehicle.
The offending vehicle hit towards the road side tree result of which this tragic incident has occurred.

Had the driver driven the offending vehicle in a moderate speed by taking all cautions,
this accident would not have occurred.
15. Hence, the materials placed on record clearly proves the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle in which deceased had not played any role.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P.5, Ex.P8 and Ex.P12.

On going through the medical documents,
it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 16-09-2024 to 30-09-2024 at T R Hospital & Research Foundation, Trichy-20 and then he was admitted at Kauvery Hospital from 27-05-2025 to 29-05- 2025.

entities.text: T R Hospital & Research Foundation, Trichy-20
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In all for a period of 18 days he has taken treatment as an inpatient.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained two injuries which are grievous in nature.
17. Dr.Nagaraj B N - Orthopaedic surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Senter at SOADS, Bangalore is examined as Pw2 and through him clinical report and X- ray film are marked as Ex.P.14 and Ex.P15.
The P.W.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 16-08- 2025 clinically, radiologically for assessment of disability.
The PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of left arm at 59% and on whole body at 20%.

PW.2 has further deposed that petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implants the estimation of surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
18.

In the cross examination, PW.2 has admitted that he has not given any treatment to the petitioner and that the fracture is united and that there is improvement in the health condition of the petitioner and that the injuries sustained by the petitioner would not come in the way of the education of the petitioner and that the implant is at the stage of removal.
19.
As per the case of the petitioner at the time of the accident he was pursuing 1st semester in MBA.

As per the own admission of the petitioner there was no loss of Academic carrier but PW.1 deposed that due to the injuries sustained by him he could not attend one exam but no document has been Kamalesh S vs Ramesh M on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22645315/
4 produced to say that due to the injuries sustained by the petitioner, he could not attend the one exam.
In the petition it is stated that petitioner was doing part time job in Medical store and earning sum of Rs..20,000/ but no document to that effect has been produced.
The petitioner being MBA student, there is no possibility of his doing part time job work along with his education.
Though the PW.2 has assessed the disability of the petitioner on whole body at 20% but when 1/3 rd of the disability on particular body is taken as disability of whole body, it comes around 16%.

But since petitioner is person of young age aged about 20 years and since fracture is united and there is improvement in the health condition, it can be said that PW.2 has assessed the disability on higher side.
Hence this court inclines to consider the disability at 10%.
But 10% of disability would not affect the future earnings of the petitioner.
At the most the said percentage of disability would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.

Hence petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort but not under the head loss of income during the laid down period and under loss of future income due to the disability suffered by him.
20. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
21. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering.
22. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has produced medical bills for Rs.4,06,239/- and for Rs.1,24,490/- at Ex.P10 and Ex.P14.

If the medical bills for Rs. 4,06,239/- as per Ex.P10 produced by the petitioner is carefully perused wherein bill no.195 for Rs. 20,000/- bill no.188 for Rs.10,000/- and bill no.240 for Rs.20,000/- are the advance receipts and the said amounts are included in bill no.61/24 (serial no.1 in Ex.P10).
Further in serial no.1, bill no.61/24, room charges are included but the petitioner has produced bill no.343 towards room charges.
Further bill no.194 for Rs.2,400/- includes Rs.400/- towards registration charges.
The said amount of Rs.400/- is included in bill no.61/24.
Hence out of Rs.4,06,239/- which is the amount calculated by the petitioner, sum of Rs. 90,100/- has to be deducted.
On such deduction it comes around Rs.3,16,139/-.
So far as medical bill as per Ex.P14 for Rs.1,24,490/- produced by the petitioner is concerned, pharmacy bill of sum of Rs.19,592/- is included in bill no.1581.
Hence out of Rs.1,24,490/- sum of Rs.19,592/- has to be deducted.
On such deduction the medical expenses incurred as per Ex.P14 would come around Rs. 1,04,898/-.
Thus the petitioner has incurred medical expenses to the tune of Rs.3,16,139/- + Rs.1,04,898/- = Rs. 4,21,037/-.
As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,21,037/- under the head medical expenses.
23. It is stated that petitioner was aged about 20 years.

He was student of Ist semester MBA pursuing Jain CMS Business School, Sheshadri road, Bangalore and also doing part time work at medical store/stationary ship, Bengaluru and earning sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But the petitioner has not produced any document to prove that he was studying MBA Ist semester and doing part time work at medical store.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities, discomfort and loss of academic career to the tune of Rs.2,00,000/-.
25.
So far as the future medical expenses for removal of implant is concerned, PW.2 has deposed that petitioner requires Rs.60,000/- for future medical expenses.
But he has not given any estimation
Hence, this court awards compensation under the head future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/-.
26. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at T R Hospital & Research Foundation, Trichy-20 and Kauvery Hospital K.C General Hospital.

He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore, this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.7,61,037 (Rupees Seven Lakhs Sixty One Thousand Thirty Seven only).
27.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with 2 nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no 2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
28. Issue No.3:

ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
